reproduction_target: Computational re-analysis of published murine liver TCDD/AHR genomics data: (a) ChIP-seq re-processing (trim_galore -> bowtie2 mm10 -> MACS2 peaks -> bedtools merge) of AHR datasets GSE97634/GSE97636, followed by AHR motif (XRE/NC-XRE) scanning with an in-house script, random-control enrichment (Fisher exact), ChromHMM 10-state chromatin annotation over 9 ENCODE histone-mark tracks, HOMER signal/motif enrichment, and motif-run detection; (b) RNA-seq re-processing (trim_galore -> STAR mm10 -> feature_counts -> EdgeR+RUVr DEGs) of GSE109863/GSE62902/GSE87519, GSEA (MSigDB v7.5.1), and custom Over-Representation Analysis (Rajapakshe & Coarfa ORA v4.0; GO BP v7.5.1, CollecTRI v2). Wet-lab validation (CRISPR editing of the Serpine1 5x NC-XRE in Hepa 1-6 cells + qRT-PCR) is out of the computational reproduction target.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from Methods prose. Computational re-analysis relies on standard public tools (trim_galore, bowtie2, MACS2, bedtools, STAR, feature_counts, EdgeR, RUVr, ChromHMM, HOMER, eulerr, GSEA) plus several unshared in-house/custom scripts (AHR motif search, random-control generation, motif-run detection, ORA v4.0). No code-availability statement and no repository (GitHub/GitLab/Zenodo/SoftwareHeritage) found in paper prose. Data are reused public GEO accessions. Wet-lab steps (cell culture, FACS cloning, CRISPR, genotyping, qRT-PCR) counted as W, excluded from S. Stage-1 prose only; no workflow source read.

steps.label: ChIP-seq read trimming (trim_galore) of AHR datasets GSE97634/GSE97636 downloaded from GEO
AHR motif (XRE/NC-XRE) scanning within peaks using an in-house script (not shared)
Random-control peak generation matched to chromosome/size distribution 'as previously described' (Coarfa 2020); code/parameters not provided
Motif enrichment vs random (Fisher exact, p<0.05) and Venn diagrams (eulerr package in R/RStudio)
Chromatin-state annotation: trim_galore+bowtie2 of 9 ENCODE histone-mark tracks (GSM1000140 etc.), then ChromHMM 10-state HMM segmentation overlaid on AHR peaks (overlay via custom in-house script)
Histone-mark signal distributions across genomic regions and flanking-sequence motif enrichment (HOMER)
Detection of AHR motif runs (successive motifs within max distance) using an in-house Python script + bedtools; script not shared
RNA-seq read trimming (trim_galore) of GSE109863/GSE62902/GSE87519 from GEO
Differential expression (EdgeR + RUVr), FC>1.5x and FDR<0.05
Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) on ranked gene list using MSigDB mouse collection v7.5.1
Over-Representation Analysis via custom Python script (Rajapakshe & Coarfa ORA v4.0; hypergeometric test) against GO BP v7.5.1 and CollecTRI v2 regulons; script not shared

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 12 of 16 computational steps (standard public tools run on public GEO data, reproducible-in-principle but with no version pins, no exact commands/parameters, and no environment closure). 4 steps (C5 AHR-motif scan, C6 random-control generation, C10 motif-run detection, C16 ORA v4.0) drop to NI because they depend on in-house/custom scripts that are not deposited and have no code-availability statement or repository. capture_claim is 'floating' (a few isolated version tokens — MSigDB v7.5.1, CollecTRI v2, ORA v4.0, GraphPad Prism 10.2.2 — but no env lock, lockfile, container, or repo), so this paper is NOT a stage2 R★ candidate: even a perfect stage2 run could not exceed RI.
headline.coverage: 16 computational steps assessed from Methods prose across two re-analysis pipelines (ChIP-seq C1-C10, RNA-seq C11-C16). 5 wet-lab steps (W=5: cell culture, FACS cloning, CRISPR mutagenesis, genotyping, qRT-PCR) present but outside the computational reproduction target. No code repository located in paper prose.

gaps.where: Custom/in-house analysis code (steps C5, C6, C10, C16)
gaps.missing: No code-availability statement and no repository (GitHub/GitLab/Zenodo/Software Heritage) found. Multiple analyses rely on unshared in-house scripts: AHR motif scanning, random-control peak generation, motif-run detection, and the Rajapakshe & Coarfa ORA v4.0 Python script. Chromatin-state overlay onto AHR peaks also uses a 'custom in-house script'.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit all in-house/custom scripts (motif scanner, random-control generator, motif-run detector, ORA v4.0, overlay scripts) in a versioned, licensed repository with a Zenodo/tagged snapshot cited in the paper.

gaps.missing: No environment.yml / lockfile / container. Core tools (trim_galore, bowtie2, MACS2, bedtools, STAR, feature_counts, EdgeR, RUVr, ChromHMM, HOMER, eulerr, GSEA) are named without version pins; R/RStudio version unspecified. Only a few isolated version tokens exist (MSigDB v7.5.1, CollecTRI v2, ORA v4.0, GraphPad Prism 10.2.2).
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/pixi.lock or container digest for a declared platform and record the exact version of every tool used.

gaps.missing: Statistical thresholds are partly given (Fisher p<0.05; DEG FC>1.5x, FDR<0.05; 10 kb peak-to-gene window; 10 ChromHMM states), but tool-level parameters (trim_galore/bowtie2/MACS2/STAR/feature_counts/HOMER command lines, MACS2 control mapping, motif-run max-distance) are not specified.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide exact command lines / parameter settings for each tool, and the max-distance definition for motif runs.

gaps.missing: Primary inputs are reused public GEO accessions (GSE97634, GSE97636, GSE109863, GSE62902, GSE87519, and 9 ENCODE histone GSMs) which are provided — good. However no processed/intermediate artifacts (peak/BED files, count matrices, motif catalogs, ChromHMM segmentations) are deposited, and the random-control set is defined only 'as previously described'.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit processed BED/peak files, count matrices, motif tables, and ChromHMM segmentations (e.g., Zenodo) with a manifest keyed to each figure.

gaps.missing: No repository, tagged release, DOI snapshot, or license exists for any of the analysis code; there is no citable software artifact at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Create an OSI-licensed repository with a tagged release / Zenodo DOI and cite the specific commit in the paper.
